# Client Statements in a Therapy Session

## Background Context
*Sarah is a 34-year-old marketing executive who recently received a promotion she didn't want. She's been married for 7 years to James, a surgeon who works long hours. They have a 4-year-old daughter, Emma. Sarah's mother passed away three years ago from cancer, and her father has been struggling with grief. Sarah grew up in a high-achievement household where emotional expression was discouraged. She has been experiencing depression and anxiety for approximately 18 months, with symptoms worsening over the past four months.*

---

## The 100 Statements

1. "I don't even know why I'm here. Nothing ever really changes anyway."

2. "James thinks I'm overreacting. He says everyone gets stressed at work."

3. "I used to love my job, but now I can't even get out of bed on Mondays."

4. "My dad called yesterday and I just couldn't answer. I don't have the energy to hear him talk about how much he misses Mom."

5. "Emma asked me why Mommy is always sad, and I just... I didn't know what to say."

6. "I had a panic attack in the bathroom at work last Tuesday, and nobody even noticed."

7. "Sometimes I think everyone would be better off without me."

8. "I keep replaying conversations from years ago, wondering if people actually like me."

9. "When I was promoted, I felt like a fraud. I still feel like a fraud."

10. "I can't remember the last time I slept through the night without waking up in a cold sweat."

11. "My mother would be so disappointed in me right now."

12. "I have this constant feeling in my chest, like something terrible is about to happen."

13. "I used to be the person who had everything figured out, and now I can't figure out anything."

14. "James makes more money than me, so I feel like I should be doing more at home, but I'm too exhausted."

15. "I haven't called my best friend in three weeks. I feel too ashamed."

16. "What if I'm just fundamentally broken?"

17. "My boss pulled me aside yesterday and asked if I was okay. Apparently, I seem 'distracted.'"

18. "I look in the mirror and don't recognize myself anymore."

19. "I lie awake at night making lists of all the ways I'm failing."

20. "My mother used to say that feelings were a sign of weakness. Maybe she was right."

21. "Sometimes I have these intrusive thoughts about horrible things happening to Emma, and it terrifies me."

22. "I feel guilty for feeling depressed when I have a good life on paper."

23. "The medication my last doctor prescribed made me feel numb, so I stopped taking it."

24. "I can't concentrate on anything anymore. I read the same paragraph five times."

25. "Everyone expects me to be the strong one, the one who has it together."

26. "I've been having tension headaches for months. My doctor said it's stress-related."

27. "I don't remember what it felt like to be happy."

28. "My sister told me I should just 'think positive,' and I wanted to scream."

29. "I'm angry all the time, but I don't know what I'm angry at."

30. "Sometimes I feel like I'm watching my life from outside my body."

31. "I've started avoiding my work meetings because I'm terrified I'll have another panic attack."

32. "My father keeps saying he doesn't know how to help me, which somehow makes me feel even more alone."

33. "I used to exercise regularly, but now even the thought of going to the gym is overwhelming."

34. "I feel like I'm drowning, and everyone is just watching."

35. "When did I become this person who can't handle basic things?"

36. "I think James is having second thoughts about our marriage."

37. "I have these thoughts that everyone is talking about me behind my back."

38. "My doctor suggested that my anxiety might be connected to the unresolved grief about my mom, but I don't see how."

39. "I can't eat normally anymore. Some days I forget to eat entirely, and other days I can't stop."

40. "I feel like I'm disappointing Emma by not being the mother she deserves."

41. "I had a moment yesterday where I just sat on the kitchen floor and cried for an hour."

42. "Sometimes I wonder if I got the promotion because they were just being nice, not because I deserved it."

43. "I'm terrified of dying, which sounds crazy because I'm only 34."

44. "My neck and shoulders are constantly tense. It's like my body is stuck in fight-or-flight mode."

45. "I can't shake the feeling that I'm fundamentally unlovable."

46. "I used to be ambitious, but now I just feel... empty."

47. "When James tries to comfort me, I just feel more anxious because I feel like I'm burdening him."

48. "I've been having recurring dreams about my mother's funeral."

49. "I'm worried that if I actually get better, people will expect more from me."

50. "I can't stop checking my work emails, even at midnight, worried I'm messing something up."

51. "My mother never taught me how to process difficult emotions because she never did it herself."

52. "I feel like I'm a completely different person than I was two years ago."

53. "I had a panic attack during Emma's school play, and I had to leave early."

54. "I feel guilty for not being there for my dad more since Mom died."

55. "Sometimes I think about calling in sick to work, but then I feel guilty about leaving the team."

56. "I've lost interest in things I used to love, like reading and painting."

57. "I'm exhausted all the time, but I can't sleep."

58. "I keep thinking that maybe everyone would be happier if I just disappeared."

59. "I have this constant voice in my head telling me I'm not good enough."

60. "When I see other mothers at pickup, I feel like they're all judging me for not being cheerful."

61. "I don't know how to ask for help without feeling like I'm being a burden."

62. "I've been white-knuckling through life for so long that I don't know how to just be anymore."

63. "My anxiety makes me feel like I have to control everything, but I can't control anything."

64. "I wonder if this is just who I am now, and maybe it's never going to get better."

65. "I had a moment of panic yesterday when I couldn't remember what Emma looks like for a second."

66. "My performance review is coming up, and I'm terrified."

67. "I feel disconnected from my body, like it belongs to someone else."

68. "I used to be fun and spontaneous, and now I'm just... rigid."

69. "I'm worried that if I talk about my feelings, James will think I'm weak."

70. "I can feel my heart racing for no reason at all."

71. "I had a thought today that maybe everyone would be better off if I wasn't here."

72. "I don't know how to explain to my boss why I need time off without telling them about my depression."

73. "I keep having nightmares about not being able to protect Emma from something bad."

74. "My mother always said we don't air our dirty laundry, so I don't talk to anyone about what's going on."

75. "I feel like I'm faking it every single day, pretending everything is fine."

76. "I've noticed I'm more irritable with James and Emma lately, and I hate myself for it."

77. "I feel like I'm in a fog that I can't get out of, no matter what I do."

78. "I'm terrified that I'm going to pass this anxiety down to Emma somehow."

79. "Sometimes I think about not waking up, and that scares me more than anything."

80. "I used to feel confident in my decisions, but now I second-guess everything."

81. "I'm worried that my depression is going to cost me my marriage."

82. "I had a moment where I thought, 'Why am I even trying?'"

83. "I feel like there's a weight on my chest that never goes away."

84. "I don't know if I can do this anymore."

85. "My hands shake when I'm in meetings now."

86. "I feel like I'm supposed to be stronger than this."

87. "I don't know who to trust with how I'm really feeling."

88. "I feel like my anxiety is irrational, which makes me even more anxious."

89. "I can't remember the last time I felt truly relaxed."

90. "I'm worried that talking about this makes it real, makes it permanent."

91. "I feel like I'm losing myself and I don't know how to get back."

92. "Sometimes I dissociate during conversations, and I don't even realize it's happening until someone asks me a question."

93. "I'm afraid that if I stop being productive, I'll have no value."

94. "I feel like my mother's death opened something in me that can never be closed again."

95. "I wonder if I even deserve to feel better."

96. "I'm terrified of taking medication because what if I become someone I don't recognize?"

97. "I feel like I'm a burden to everyone around me."

98. "I don't know when I started believing I wasn't good enough, but I can't seem to stop believing it now."

99. "I feel like if I admit I need help, I'm giving up."

100. "I don't know if I can get through another day like yesterday, but I'm too afraid to say that out loud to anyone but you."

---

## Notes on These Statements

These statements reflect common themes in depression and anxiety:
- **Guilt and shame** (statements 15, 22, 25, 40)
- **Suicidal ideation** (statements 7, 58, 79, 84)
- **Grief and loss** (statements 4, 11, 48, 94)
- **Identity disruption** (statements 13, 18, 52, 68, 91)
- **Physical symptoms** (statements 10, 26, 45, 70, 85)
- **Relationship concerns** (statements 2, 14, 36, 47, 81)
- **Catastrophic thinking** (statements 21, 63, 78)
- **Perfectionism and achievement pressure** (statements 9, 25, 49, 93)
- **Avoidance behaviors** (statements 15, 31, 55)
- **Feeling of hopelessness** (statements 1, 46, 64, 88, 90)
